invariants.rationale: x is a boolean, so it must always be either true or false.
y is a boolean, so it must always be either true or false.
x and y are both booleans, so for any execution they are either equal or not, which exhausts all possibilities.
If x is true and y is false, then (x || y) must be true, which is always the case for booleans.
The law of excluded middle for boolean variables, always true for boolean values.
